verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission to leave Earth’s orbit and journey to the vicinity of the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'More than half a century after the final Apollo lunar mission'; R2: 'first time astronauts return to the vicinity of the moon in more than 50 years'; R3: 'For the first time in over 50 years, astronauts from Earth have launched to the moon'; R6: 'humanity's first lunar voyage in more than half a century'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state it is the first crewed mission to the Moon vicinity in over 50 years since Apollo (1972).

verifications.claim: Artemis II launches in April 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'April 1'; R2: 'April 1 launch'; R3: 'April 1, 2026'; R4: 'April 1'; R5: 'LaunchED April 1, 2026'; R6: 'April 1, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources confirm launch on April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a 10-day test mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day journey'; R2: '10 days'; R3: '10-day journey'; R4: 'roughly 10-day flight'; R5: 'MISSION DURATION 9 Days, 1 Hour, 32 Minutes' (approx 10 days); R6: 'less than 10 days'; R7: 'historic 10-day journey'
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as a ~10-day test flight across sources.

verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm it sets new distance record for humans.

verifications.claim: Artemis III will land astronauts at the lunar South Pole.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R1: 'uncrewed Artemis III mission, which is expected to touch down near the moon’s... south pole' (contradicts astronauts); R3: 'Artemis 3 in 2027 — an Earth-orbit flight' (no landing); R4: 'plans to land astronauts near the moon's south pole' (vague, not specific to III)
verifications.reasoning: R1 contradicts by specifying uncrewed; others do not confirm crewed landing on III.

verifications.reasoning: Sources link Artemis to Mars goals broadly, but not specific systems testing for Mars.

verifications.claim: Artemis II crew will validate life support systems needed for long-term human presence in space.
